correctness.rationale: C PASS: In the canonical unweighted cycle C_n, n>=3, the n Laplacian columns affinely span the zero-sum hyperplane. Its barycentric facet normals are L_n^+e_i. Directly solving both cyclic difference equations gives (L_n^+)^2_{00}=(n^2-1)(n^2+11)/(720n) and (L_n^+)^2_{00}-(L_n^+)^2_{0d}=d(n-d)[d(n-d)+2]/(24n); their normalized Gram cosine gives the exact claimed interior dihedral angle pi-arccos(1-30u(u+2)/D_n). Increasing u over 1..floor(n/2) proves levels and multiplicities, with n=3,4 acute and n>=5 both signs. Exact angular distribution follows the distance-pair Riemann sum, and integrated cosine moments give 1/(n-1), 3/7. Independent rational matrix inversions and directly reconstructed normals were checked for n=3..12; finite instances corroborate rather than prove all n.

originality.rationale: O PASS, best of knowledge: The same Euclidean realization and pseudoinverse facet-normal formula, and even the cycle diagonal norm/inradius, are known in the earlier vertex-transitive Laplacian-simplex theorem. That full proof was inspected. Its scalar spectral trace supplies only squared normal lengths, not their off-diagonal Gram matrix, distance-indexed full angle multiset or sharp acute/obtuse asymptotic. Braun-Meyer and Meyer-Pllaha focus on lattice/Ehrhart/coding invariants; Devriendt provides broader generic Gram angle machinery for a differing graph simplex model. The evaluated all-cycle angle spectrum and limiting law were not identified as earlier stated implications. Biharmonic Green-function tables and alternative angular nomenclature remain a priority risk.
